Key Activities: Plans and directs major economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and writes/presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience.
Provides expert analysis and advice to senior officials at all levels of government, industry, academia, other national and international institutions and special interest groups.
Develops new methods and techniques to meet the needs of the most unique studies and assesses the implications of new approaches.
Oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and determines departmental impact and implications.
Manages the work of multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams involved in research and analytical activities.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.

1. Decision making: Plans and directs major economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research covering a range of departmental statistical programs; proposes new approaches and develops solutions or enhancements to methodology; selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs. Coordinates non-recurring research studies covering issues impacting on major departmental entities across government.
Recommends new research initiatives to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels.

Reviews and evaluates statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the use and application of departmental statistical programs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams involved in research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term project goals. Allocates human and financial resource needs to achieve project objectives. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff.

Plans and manages budgets for projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: As a subject matter expert, provides advisory and consultative services to senior officials within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of major economic and socio-economic studies and research and their impact on complex issues.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex research results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of research findings. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of research and analysis, it is necessary to further explain the results, methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.

Provides expert advice and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the results of research and analytical studies, economic / social science theories and principles and statistical concepts and methods.

Consults with officials of other government departments, industries and special interest groups, to ensure that their priorities and interests, and those of the department, are considered in the departmental decision making process. Broader government wide objectives must also be considered.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociological theories and principles especially as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the specialized area. This is necessary to initiate and conduct research and analytical projects to improve upon existing or develop new concepts, and to assess the content of articles and reports that will be distributed widely or published.
Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Knowledge of resource and project management practices and principles in order to manage project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program.

Knowledge of divisional mandate, policies, priorities, practices, standards and procedures as well as existing databases and conceptual frameworks applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical projects and to determine or recommend changes.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic research and studies on complex policy issues impacting on major departmental entities across government, industry, academia and other national and international organizations. This includes determining the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work and organizing the review and presentation of findings.

Plans and implements new research initiatives to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, plans and develops a program of review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the use and application of departmental statistical programs.

Presents options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders, directs major cross-sectoral and inter-departmental studies and provides expert analysis and advice to senior officials at all levels of government, industry, and academia, other national and international institutions and special interest groups.
